briefdescription.para: KnownFeasibleEdges - Entries in this set are edges which have already had PHI nodes retriggered.

GlobalValue - If we are tracking any values for the contents of a global variable, we keep a mapping from the constant accessor to the element of the global, to the currently known value.

detaileddescription.para: If the value becomes overdefined, it's entry is simply removed from this map.

briefdescription.para: TrackedRetVals - If we are tracking arguments into and the return value out of a function, it will have an entry in this map, indicating what the known return value for the function is.
TrackedMultipleRetVals - Same as TrackedRetVals, but used for functions that return multiple values.

A list of functions whose return cannot be modified.
TrackingIncomingArguments - This is the set of functions for whose arguments we make optimistic assumptions about and try to prove as constants.
The reason for two worklists is that overdefined is the lowest state on the lattice, and moving things to overdefined as fast as possible makes SCCP converge much faster.

detaileddescription.para: By having a separate worklist, we accomplish this because everything possibly overdefined will become overdefined at the soonest possible point.

briefdescription.para: While solving the dataflow for a function, we don't compute a result for operations with an undef operand, to allow undef to be lowered to a constant later.

detaileddescription.para: For example, constant folding of "zext i8 undef to i16" would result in "i16 0", and if undef is later lowered to "i8 1", then the zext result would become "i16 1" and would result into an overdefined lattice value once merged with the previous result. Not computing the result of the zext (treating undef the same as unknown) allows us to handle a later undef->constant lowering more optimally.

However, if the operand remains undef when the solver returns, we do need to assign some result to the instruction (otherwise we would treat it as unreachable). For simplicity, we mark any instructions that are still unknown as overdefined.
